description: Biz, Muğla merkezli; uzay teknolojileri, simülasyon, oyun geliştirme ve UI/UX alanlarında yenilikçi projeler üreten tutkulu bir ekibiz. Python, Flutter ve 3D oyun motorlarıyla interaktif uygulamalar ve uzay mekaniği simülasyonları geliştiriyoruz.
summary:
APOGEE is an interactive 2.5D isometric space mission simulator that teaches how real missions are designed. Players act as mission architects: they choose a target (Moon, Mars, Europa or Earth orbit), build a spacecraft from realistic subsystems (propulsion, power, communications, instruments, thermal), pick a launcher, and then fly the mission live.

Many students find orbital mechanics abstract and intimidating. APOGEE turns it into a game loop that still uses real physics: the Tsiolkovsky rocket equation, Lambert transfer solutions shown as an interactive porkchop plot for choosing launch windows, a 4th-order Runge-Kutta orbit propagator, link budgets for NASA’s Deep Space Network, and a 1,000-run Monte Carlo risk analysis. The game also pulls live NASA space-weather data (DONKI) and Earth-distance data (JPL Horizons), so solar storms and signal delay can affect a mission.

After each flight, players see a debrief that compares their design with real NASA missions such as LRO, MAVEN and Europa Clipper. APOGEE is bilingual (English/Turkish), works offline, and runs as a website or a desktop app. It makes mission design accessible, engaging and educational for students.
details:
What it does and how it works
APOGEE guides the player through a complete mission life cycle:

  1. Mission selection and design: The player chooses a mission and builds a spacecraft in an isometric cleanroom. Mass, power, thermal, delta-v and communication margins update live.
  2. Pre-launch review: A 1,000-run seeded Monte Carlo analysis estimates mission reliability and gives a GO / CAUTION / NO-GO status. It also gives a “what if” tip, e.g. “+10% delta-v”. A Flight Director panel critiques the design.
  3. Launch window planning (Theory Lab): An interactive porkchop plot (departure date × time of flight), computed with a Universal Variable Lambert solver, lets players pick a real transfer window. The chosen window sets the mission’s required delta-v.
  4. Live flight: The spacecraft is propagated with an RK4 integrator. Players can plan prograde, retrograde and radial maneuvers, preview the predicted trajectory, and see propellant use calculated with the Tsiolkovsky equation. Mars and Europa missions use a Sun-centred 3D cruise and a two-burn orbit insertion.
  5. Debrief and progression: The score is shown transparently, and the design is compared with real reference missions. Earnings are reinvested in R&D, a fleet and a 2.5D space habitat.

Benefits and intended impact
APOGEE helps students and space enthusiasts understand systems engineering trade-offs (mass vs. power vs. cost vs. risk) by experiencing them, not just reading about them. We hope it inspires young people, especially in Türkiye, to consider careers in space science and engineering.

NASA data and honesty about limits
The game queries NASA DONKI (coronal mass ejections) and JPL Horizons (Earth range and light-time). When offline, it clearly labels fallback data as “Sample Archive”. APOGEE is an educational simulator, not flight software; all model limits are documented in docs/PHYSICS.md and docs/ENGINEERING_AUDIT.md.

Tools and technologies
TypeScript, React, Vite, Tailwind CSS, HTML5 Canvas (custom isometric renderer), Node.js/Express backend, Electron (desktop version), Vitest (120 automated tests covering physics, economy, security and full-app flows).

Creativity
We combined a game-like isometric world with real aerospace mathematics, deterministic seeded randomness (no Math.random()), live NASA data, and an honest, educational design. Our team is made up of 10th-grade students who wanted to make orbital mechanics fun and understandable for their peers.
